editorial:
Imagine a lonely kid in Australia and a lonely adult in New York finding comfort through letters. That is the heart of this story, and it pulls you in with its odd, sweet charm. Mary is a curious eight-year-old who feels out of place, while Max is a large, anxious man who struggles with daily life. Their friendship grows through funny, honest letters that cover everything from chocolate to big life questions. The stop-motion style gives every scene a handmade feel, and the gray, brown, and red color palette makes the world feel both sad and warm. It is quirky, emotional, and surprisingly funny without trying too hard.

The voice work is strong, especially the dry humor in Max’s letters, and the pacing keeps you interested even when the story gets heavy. The movie handles loneliness and mental health with care, though some moments may feel too sad for younger viewers. If you like character-driven stories, animation with heart, or bittersweet comedies, this is a great pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Mary travels to New York after years apart and finds that Max has died. She discovers he kept every letter she ever sent, along with small treasures from their friendship, showing he forgave her and valued her deeply. The ending is bittersweet but comforting, because their bond outlasts distance, mistakes, and time, and it leaves you feeling both sad and hopeful.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt animation and character-driven stories.
